Definition: adverb from a derivative of G142 (compare G740) through the idea of suspension; just now:--this day (hour), hence(-forth), here(-after), hither(-to), (even) now, (this) present.
BiblicalUsage: Now is the word for this moment, and it is used for the present that will not wait. Jesus tells John to suffer it to be so now, that all righteousness may be fulfilled, and Paul says for now we see through a glass darkly, but then face to face.
TheologicalSignificance: One small word for now carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the tension in it, that now is the time for obedience and for seeing dimly, and then is the time for seeing face to face.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
